SWE.name: Sweden
SWE.story: The post that started it all holds up: ~$211B standing, with Spotify and Ericsson still ~60% of the total.

ISR.name: Israel
ISR.story: The nation without a giant: its two biggest companies ever — Wiz ($32B) and CyberArk ($25B) — were both acquired in the past year, and no independent survivor tops ~$30B.

NLD.name: Netherlands
NLD.story: A semiconductor monoculture: ASML alone is ~80% of standing value, and chips overall are ~95%.

USA.name: United States
USA.story: The yardstick: ~$26T standing — NVIDIA alone outweighs every other country on this map combined.

CAN.name: Canada
CAN.story: Shopify and Constellation are 80% of the total; the biggest exit ever (Slack) was born in Vancouver, built in San Francisco.

GBR.name: United Kingdom
GBR.story: Far ahead of the continent — Arm plus a fintech armada — but Arm is ~90% SoftBank-owned and the icons (DeepMind, Darktrace, Deliveroo) sold abroad.

DEU.name: Germany
DEU.story: Europe's largest economy, one giant: SAP and Infineon are ~80% of the total — and Germany almost never sells.

FRA.name: France
FRA.story: Engineering-rich, breakout-poor: the biggest pure software company dates to 1977, and the hopes ride on Mistral.

FIN.name: Finland
FIN.story: Nokia is back (~$57B) — and the entire second act (Supercell, Wolt, Rovio, WithSecure) got sold.

DNK.name: Denmark
DNK.story: Copenhagen founds them, San Francisco scales them — Unity and Zendesk were both born here.

NOR.name: Norway
NOR.story: One quiet giant nobody abroad can name — Visma (~$22B) — and this month's Cognite sale was the biggest exit ever.

EST.name: Estonia
EST.story: Skype's engineers were Tallinn's — the alumni seeded Europe's densest startup scene. Wise (counted for the UK) and Bolt carry the flag.

IRL.name: Ireland
IRL.story: Ireland exports founders, not companies: Stripe ($159B) and Intercom were built by Irishmen in San Francisco. Count them and Ireland rivals Israel — this map doesn't, and that gap IS the story.

CHE.name: Switzerland
CHE.story: Quiet B2B depth — and most 'Swiss' giants on the lists (TE Connectivity, Garmin, STMicro) aren't Swiss-founded at all.

ESP.name: Spain
ESP.story: Amadeus — the giant nobody calls tech — is three-quarters of the scoreboard.

POL.name: Poland
POL.story: Poland IPOs at home instead of selling — and its biggest 'tech company', ElevenLabs ($11B), was founded by Poles abroad, so it doesn't count here. That gap is the story.

CHN.name: China
CHN.story: The walled garden: ~$2.2T standing and effectively zero realized — capital controls mean China's tech is never for sale.

JPN.name: Japan
JPN.story: The quiet superpower: five chip-equipment makers outweigh Sony and Nintendo combined — and nothing is ever sold. Japan's top startup (Sakana AI) is just $2.7B.

KOR.name: South Korea
KOR.story: The memory duopoly ate the card: Samsung + SK Hynix are ~$2T of the $2.2T total. The biggest exit ever was domestic — Naver buying crypto exchange Dunamu.

TWN.name: Taiwan
TWN.story: The indispensable island: $2.9T standing — the highest per-capita tech value on Earth (~$128K/person, double the US).

IND.name: India
IND.story: IT services built most of the card — and AI is eating it (TCS halved). Consumer tech IPOs at home; the one mega-exit was Flipkart to Walmart.

RUS.name: Russia
RUS.story: The scoreboard sanctions built: the global halves left (Nebius, Telegram), Wildberries can't be priced, and what's listed is worth less than Estonia's startups. Ruble caps are not internationally comparable.

TUR.name: Turkey
TUR.story: Istanbul makes games and apps; the wins sell early (Peak, Trendyol's majority went for $728M) and the unicorns deflate — Getir fell from $11.8B to a $335M asset sale.

ARE.name: UAE
ARE.story: The Gulf's hub imports its giants: Telegram — founded by a Russian, run from Dubai — is half the card. Careem remains the only big homegrown exit.

BRA.name: Brazil
BRA.story: Fintech nation: Nubank is two-thirds of the card, and eight of nine anchors are payments or banking apps.

ARG.name: Argentina
ARG.story: MercadoLibre is 95% of the card — Latin America's giant is Argentine. Auth0's founders were Argentine too, but it was born in Seattle (excluded by our rule).

AUS.name: Australia
AUS.story: SaaS islands: Canva ($42B) has overtaken Atlassian — and the biggest exit (Afterpay, $29B) sold at the very top of the market.

SGP.name: Singapore
SGP.story: The hub: Sea and Grab both fly Singapore's flag — one born here, one adopted from Malaysia under the same headcount rule we use everywhere.

ITA.name: Italy
ITA.story: Italy's two giants came out of nowhere: Technoprobe's chip test-cards and Bending Spoons' app empire, which IPO'd this month at $21B.

PRT.name: Portugal
PRT.story: Portugal founds and keeps (OutSystems, Sword, Feedzai) — while its most famous 'Portuguese' companies, Farfetch and Talkdesk, were born abroad and don't count.

GRC.name: Greece
GRC.story: Greece's first unicorn sold 48.5% to JPMorgan and kept its flag by half a percent.

AUT.name: Austria
AUT.story: Dynatrace, born in Linz, is half the card; Bitpanda's Frankfurt IPO keeps slipping.

HUN.name: Hungary
HUN.story: Hungary sells: LogMeIn's $4.3B exit is four times everything Budapest still owns.

SVK.name: Slovakia
SVK.story: ESET is Slovakia: founder-owned since 1992, never priced by any market. (Estimate shown.)

CZE.name: Czechia
CZE.story: Bootstrapped Prague: JetBrains (~$7B, never raised a dollar) — and Avast, sold for $8.6B.

ROU.name: Romania
ROU.story: UiPath: from a Bucharest apartment to a $35B peak — and back to $6B. Still Romania's whole card.

BGR.name: Bulgaria
BGR.story: Payhawk carries the flag Telerik planted.

UKR.name: Ukraine
UKR.story: Wartime resilience: Grammarly, Preply, and Ajax — all Kyiv-born, all still growing through the war. GitLab began in Ukrainian code but grew up American (excluded).

LTU.name: Lithuania
LTU.story: Vilnius quietly built Vinted (€8B) and NordVPN. Wargaming's biggest studio is here — but it was born in Minsk, so it doesn't count.

LVA.name: Latvia
LVA.story: One unicorn card: Fyul, the Printful-Printify print-on-demand merger — Latvia's first and only.

HRV.name: Croatia
HRV.story: Infobip — a $10B messaging giant from Vodnjan, population six thousand — plus the math app Google bought.

SRB.name: Serbia
SRB.story: Serbia ships engineers and games — Top Eleven's maker was the flag exit.

SVN.name: Slovenia
SVN.story: Slovenia's tech story is two exits: Talking Tom went to China for $1B, and the world's oldest crypto exchange went to Robinhood.

ISL.name: Iceland
ISL.story: EVE Online sold to Korea for $425M in 2018 — then its makers bought themselves back this May for $120M.

LUX.name: Luxembourg
LUX.story: Luxembourg hosts — Skype was run from here — but it doesn't found. An honest zero.

BEL.name: Belgium
BEL.story: Odoo compounds quietly from Wallonia — and Aikido just became Europe's fastest-ever cybersecurity unicorn.

SAU.name: Saudi Arabia
SAU.story: State tech: Elm — the PIF's e-government arm — is ninety percent of the card; the private scene is young.

EGY.name: Egypt
EGY.story: Two fintechs carry Egypt: Fawry, the listed veteran, and MNT-Halan, the super-app heading for IPO.

ZAF.name: South Africa
ZAF.story: The scoreboard misses SA's real fortune: Naspers turned $32M into the biggest outside stake in Tencent — but a holding company isn't a tech company. What's left: Karooooo, and Shuttleworth's 1999 Thawte exit.

NGA.name: Nigeria
NGA.story: Fintech nation in waiting: five unicorns, all payments — and Paystack's $200M sale to Stripe lit the fuse.
